$comment: Ceilings for every shipped wasm artifact, read by `cargo xtask size` against the cargo artifact `cargo xtask dist wasm` ships (the release build with remapped paths, before wasm-bindgen and wasm-opt). Shrink-only: a ceiling more than the headroom above its artifact fails until lowered with `cargo xtask size --update`; raising one is a hand edit, and its reason says why the growth is worth it.

whiteboard-wasm.reason: abi_version(), the batched det exports, edge_route_on_grid from the routing spike, and the batched layer-2 test surface of each edge module ported so far (ADR-0054 step 5): the geometry and ink primitives, edge-rules, and the router's leaves (side-slides, straight-detour, edge-sides, edge-contact, bend-route over the routing wire), about 96 KB (the BTree collections the corner search and the side choice need, and eight exports), the router itself (route_edge behind one edge_route_edge export), about 55 KB, and the anchor pass (fan-out, lanes, patch, alignment behind edge_compute_anchors), about 72 KB, the coincident-ends repair behind edge_repair_coincident, about 13 KB, the crossing sweep behind edge_pairwise_scores, about 34 KB, and the side-choice search (the incremental score, the around ledger, the regions, assign_edge_anchors behind edge_assign_anchors), about 126 KB, of which about 72 KB is code spread over the search's own sorts and iterators and about 53 KB the name section this artifact still carries before wasm-bindgen strips it, and edge_route_layout, the one-call-per-layout export over both, about 5 KB, which answers the anchors beside the routes: 544794 bytes measured. Then okf_parse and okf_serialize (ADR-0054 step 6), the OKF envelope over the frontmatter YAML reader and writer, about 350 KB: 126 KB of whiteboard-codec code (the YAML reader and its schema, the writer and its quoting and folding), 31 KB of serde_json for the document wire, and the rest the name section this artifact still carries before wasm-bindgen strips it (311 KB in all); the shipped, stripped module is 520132 bytes. Production code the default will route through, not test surface: 895418 bytes measured then The router's, the anchor pass's, the repair's, the sweep's and the search's shares are production code the one-call-per-layout export ships too, not test surface; trading the partition's JsMaps or the stable sorts for smaller code was measured and saved nothing. Every released build ships this artifact (the npm tarball, the Docker image and the web site) while the default routing stays TypeScript, so only `differential` and `rust` load it; the per-module exports go when the one-call-per-layout export replaces them, which is when this ceiling is re-measured, and if the test surface keeps growing this fast it moves behind a cargo feature first. Then the OKF codec reading and writing the frontmatter types generated from contracts/model and calling whiteboard-model's named checks in place of its own copies (the model track, ADR-0054): 900888 bytes measured, 5470 more than before. The growth was measured as a whole, not broken down by symbol; the change removes duplicated predicates and adds none, so it is the generated types' layout and the cross-crate calls. Then the rest of the spatial canvas generated into whiteboard-model (nodes, edges, lines, comments, the canvas) with its named checks: 901294 bytes measured, 406 more than before; the types are not called from the codec yet, so the growth is the link-time layout of the larger crate, again not broken down by symbol. Then the writer reporting every place a value has no spelling, with its path (a fault list in place of the first refusal), and the reader looking for the host's lone-surrogate mark: 906435 bytes measured, 5141 more than before, about 6.5 KB of the shipped module; it is the cost of closing the declines the TypeScript used to answer (a refusal that names its path, a head read in place of a whole text). Then the JSON Canvas codec (whiteboard_codec::json_canvas), which no export reaches yet: 907028 bytes measured, 213 more than before (225 measured on its own before the OKF fault list landed) and one more function in the artifact; nothing in the wasm crate calls it, so the growth is again the link-time layout of the larger crate, not broken down by symbol. Then json_canvas_parse and json_canvas_serialize (ADR-0054 step 6), the JSON Canvas codec behind two exports: 1094982 bytes measured, 187954 more than the 907028 before. The codec had been in the crate since the port but nothing called it, so the linker dropped it; the exports make the reader (the JSON grammar, the wire schema, the extension buckets, the URL check), the projection and the writer reachable, and the canvas wire (the typed encode and decode of every field of the model's canvas) is new. The shipped, stripped module grew from 526644 to 632603 bytes (105959 more). Production code the default will route through, not test surface. Then the URL check answering every link host instead of declining one (the WHATWG IPv6 parser, percent-decoding a special host, the file host rule, and accepting an international or xn-- host with no forbidden code point, owner decision q50): 1096529 bytes measured, 1547 more than before. It is what lets the JSON Canvas TypeScript go without refusing links the TypeScript read, so it is production code the only reader runs. Then facet_bucket_check (ADR-0054 step 6, S8), the facet write behind one export: partitionFacetWrites and the stencil library's refusal over the bundled visual plugin's registry. 1363305 bytes measured, 266776 more than the 1096529 before; the shipped, stripped module grew from 632603 to 835344 bytes (202741 more). What arrived is the contract interpreter (the compiler of a contract's definitions and the walk that judges a payload by them, issue for issue), the engine's plugin loader and registry, the visual plugin's checks (the grapheme and colour predicates over unicode-segmentation), and 73 KB of the plugin's own files embedded as text (its manifest, the visual and engine and manifest contracts, and the theme, icon and stencil tables), which the registry parses once on the first call. It is production code the daemon's only write validator will run, not test surface: under owner decision q41 a plugin's schemas are a contract file this one interpreter judges, so a future plugin adds a file and no code to this artifact, which is why the interpreter is worth its size here rather than a generated validator per facet
